Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh and matching frame cap deliver a smooth, stable experience with good visuals; medium settings keep the game looking great while leaving headroom during busy late-game turns. The native Linux build is the most stable option.

profiles.Summary: Civilization VI runs well on the Steam Deck thanks to its native Linux build via Aspyr, making Proton largely unnecessary; it is a turn-based strategy game so frame rate matters less than stability, and the Deck's hardware comfortably exceeds the minimum requirements. The biggest performance concern is late-game turns on large maps, where CPU processing time (not GPU) can cause noticeable wait times between turns.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC system requirements, the Deck's hardware capabilities, and the game's native Linux build via Aspyr. On your first run, check performance during a leader cinematic and in a late-game turn on your chosen map size — if it feels slow, drop to the Optimal profile.

MaxBattery.Notes: Turn-based gameplay means a 30 fps cap is imperceptible during play; the low TDP and reduced GPU clock stretch battery significantly. Long AI turns on large maps are CPU-bound and unaffected by these settings.

KnownIssues: Late-game turns on large maps can cause long AI processing times regardless of graphical settings, as this is CPU-bound
Some UI text and tooltips can appear small on the 7-inch screen, though the game is Steam Deck Verified/Playable
Occasional reports of the game not launching correctly under Proton — using the native Linux build (no Proton) is generally recommended
In-App Purchases (DLC) and some multiplayer features may require additional setup or purchases

MaxPerformance.Notes: The Deck's RDNA 2 GPU comfortably handles Civ VI at native resolution and high settings; frame rate may dip slightly during leader cinematics or on very large maps, but the turn-based nature means these dips are not disruptive.

Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh and frame cap is ideal for a turn-based game — animations feel smooth and the lower power draw extends battery meaningfully. FSR from 1024x640 keeps the map readable without taxing the GPU.

profiles.Summary: Civilization VI runs well on the Steam Deck through Proton, with ProtonDB reporting a gold/trending-platinum tier and strong community confidence. Being a turn-based strategy game with modest GPU demands, the Deck handles it comfortably, though late-game turns with large civs can cause CPU-bound slowdowns.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC minimum/recommended requirements, the Deck's RDNA 2 hardware class, and the game's known turn-based CPU-bound nature. On first run, check frame pacing during a leader cinematic and during a late-game turn with many civs — those are the two stress points to watch.

MaxBattery.Notes: Turn-based gameplay means the GPU is rarely under sustained load, so a low TDP and clock are very effective here. FSR upscaling from 960x600 keeps visuals acceptable while maximizing session length.

KnownIssues: Late-game (300+ turns, large maps) turn processing times increase significantly due to CPU being the bottleneck, not GPU
Some UI text and tooltips may appear small at 1280x800 without UI scaling adjustments
Occasional Proton compatibility quirks with DLC content — GE-Proton or Proton Experimental may be needed for stability
Online multiplayer desync issues have been reported on Linux/Proton builds

MaxPerformance.Notes: Civ VI's GPU demands are modest enough that the Deck handles native 1280x800 at high settings well in early and mid game; late-game turn processing is CPU-bound regardless of graphics settings. Reduce Shadow Quality to Medium if frame pacing becomes inconsistent in large late-game sessions.
MaxPerformance.ExpectedFps: 55-60 fps (early/mid game); may dip to 45-50 fps late game
